clue.text: Elderly relative erring unfortunately not showing good spirit

parts.note: a grandma is an older family member

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests the letters of erring have gone wrong and come out jumbled
not showing tells us to leave a letter out of erring

explanation.surface: An old relative who keeps going astray isn't displaying much good spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'good spirit' looks like one phrase, but 'good' is wordplay and 'spirit' alone is the definition; 'not showing' drops the letter and 'unfortunately' scrambles the rest into RNIER.
explanation.definitionFit: Grand Marnier is a French orange-flavoured liqueur, and a liqueur is one kind of spirit.

clue.text: With top off beer guts get wobbly motion

indicators.note: the letters wobble about and settle into a new order
with its top off means the first letter of beer is dropped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: With the beer gone from the top, a drinker's paunch wobbles as he moves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With top off' removes B from BEER, leaving EER; 'get wobbly' then rearranges EER and GUTS together.
explanation.definitionFit: A gesture is a movement of the hand or body made to express something, so a motion.

clue.text: Partially curtail mental illness

indicators.note: Partially says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An instruction to limit some sickness of the mind, at least in part.
explanation.definitionFit: An ailment is a minor sickness or disorder, so a plain synonym for illness.

clue.text: News interrupting unusually dire television service

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into the middle of the other letters
unusually means the letters of dire appear in an unusual order

parts.note: N is new, so news, read as several of them, gives two Ns
a set is a television receiver

explanation.surface: A bulletin cutting into a dreadful TV programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' here is a set of crockery, not a broadcast; 'unusually' rearranges to DIER and 'interrupting' splits it after DI.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinner set is a matching collection of plates and dishes, which is what a dinner service means.

clue.text: Unprepared — and all is oddly British

indicators.note: oddly means take the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of the words

explanation.surface: Someone notes that everything strange is British and nothing was planned.
explanation.definitionFit: Ad-lib describes speech made up on the spot, without rehearsal or a script.

clue.text: Unused to outskirts of Welwyn Garden City?

parts.note: something unused is still new
taken as written

indicators.note: outskirts are the edges, so take the first and last letters of Welwyn

explanation.surface: Someone not used to the edges of Welwyn Garden City, a town north of London.
explanation.walkthrough: Welwyn Garden City is a planned town in Hertfordshire, north of London, built in the 1920s and later officially made a new town; the question mark marks the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden city is a planned settlement, the model for Britain's post-war planned towns, so an example of the type.

clue.text: I have briefly raised volume before getting sensitive

indicators.note: before places the upturned book ahead of the contraction
in a down clue, raised means the word is written upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a tome is a large book or volume
I have shortened is the contraction I've

explanation.surface: Someone turned up the sound just before becoming touchy.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'raised' means written upwards, giving EMOT; 'before' sets it ahead of the contraction.
explanation.definitionFit: Emotive means arousing strong feeling, so a sensitive or touchy matter is an emotive one.

clue.text: Best volunteer to keep goal is one who hasn't slipped up before

definitions.text: one who hasn't slipped up before

parts.note: the best comes first

indicators.note: to keep means the offer holds the goal inside it

parts.note: to volunteer is to offer
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: The finest volunteer has been put in goal in a football team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to keep' is the container signal; 'slipped up' here means broke the law, not made a mistake on the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A first offender is someone convicted of a crime for the first time, with no previous record.

clue.text: Broadcast 'Floral Dance'? No, that's settled!

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Will the Floral Dance, a Cornish folk tune, be broadcast? No, and that's final.
explanation.walkthrough: The Floral Dance is a well-known Cornish song associated with the Helston Furry Dance; 'Broadcast' rearranges FLORALDANCE plus NO.
explanation.definitionFit: Once and for all means finally and conclusively, as when a matter is declared closed.

clue.text: Hormone in wild lupins lacking source of protein

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: wild means the letters run riot into a new order
lacking means a letter is missing from lupins
the source of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Some hormone is found in wild lupins that are low in protein.
explanation.walkthrough: The leading 'in' is not a link word here: it stays unscrambled at the front. 'lacking source of' drops a letter, and 'wild' rearranges what is left of the lupins.
explanation.definitionFit: Insulin is the pancreatic hormone controlling blood sugar.

clue.text: Intelligence reduced by not working

parts.note: reduced prices are low
a computer system that is not working is down

explanation.surface: Someone's intellect has suffered from being unemployed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intelligence' looks like brainpower, but here it means information, as in military intelligence.
explanation.definitionFit: The low-down is the inside information on something, which is intelligence in the spying sense.

clue.text: Date juice

definitions.meaning: a date is a romantic partner, informally a girlfriend or boyfriend
to juice a fruit is to press or crush it

explanation.surface: Juice made from the sweet fruit of the palm.
explanation.definitionFit: A squeeze is a partner in slang, and to squeeze an orange is to juice it.

clue.text: Platitude with unusually morbid note

indicators.note: unusually means the letters of morbid appear out of their usual order

parts.note: E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A tired cliché accompanied by an oddly gloomy message.
explanation.definitionFit: A bromide is a trite, soothing remark, from the sedative of that name, so a commonplace.

clue.text: Clear deliveries ahead of time

indicators.note: ahead of puts the deliveries in front of the time

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled, or deliveries

explanation.surface: Parcels are cleared for delivery early.
explanation.walkthrough: An over is a set of six balls bowled from one end in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Something overt is done openly, so it is plain and clear to see.

clue.text: Meet in Ely perhaps with naive beginner only just old enough to drive

definitions.text: only just old enough to drive

indicators.note: in places the gathering inside the bishop's seat

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city, so an example of a bishop's see
a meet is a sporting gathering or event

indicators.note: the beginner of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An inexperienced newcomer meets someone in the cathedral city of Ely.
explanation.walkthrough: A see is a bishop's diocese; Ely is a small cathedral city in Cambridgeshire. 'Meet' is a noun here, a sports event.
explanation.definitionFit: Seventeen is the minimum age for a car licence in the UK, so the age of someone just able to drive.

clue.text: Museum the French will claim is ruin

parts.note: the V and A is the Victoria and Albert Museum in London

indicators.note: to claim is to take hold of, so the French article holds the word is

parts.note: le is French for the
taken as written

explanation.surface: A French museum will seize something and wreck it.
explanation.walkthrough: The V&A, short for the Victoria and Albert Museum in London, is spelt out in full; 'will claim' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To vandalise is to damage or deface property deliberately, so to ruin it.

clue.text: Lost for information about baroque?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: about means wrapped around, so the information surrounds the other piece

parts.note: gen is informal British slang for information
baroque decoration is over the top, abbreviated OTT

explanation.surface: Someone is stumped looking for facts about baroque art.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is British slang for information and OTT stands for over the top; 'about' puts OTT inside GEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something forgotten has been lost from memory, so lost in that sense.

clue.text: Shame about TV detective

parts.note: re means concerning or about
Inspector Morse is the Oxford detective of a long-running British TV series

explanation.surface: A scandal involving a television sleuth.
explanation.walkthrough: Inspector Morse was a popular British TV drama about an Oxford police detective.
explanation.definitionFit: Remorse is deep regret for wrongdoing, and the guilt of shame is close kin.

clue.text: Old boy's remedy may be unfamiliar

parts.note: OB is an old boy, a former pupil, and the possessive adds S
a cure is a remedy

explanation.surface: A former pupil's treatment may be one nobody has heard of.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscure means little known, so not familiar to most people.

clue.text: Barrister should be succinct

definitions.meaning: in British slang a ... is a lawyer, especially one defending in court
succinct means short and to the point

explanation.surface: Advice that a lawyer should keep his remarks concise.
explanation.definitionFit: Brief is informal for a defence lawyer and also means short, like a succinct speech.

clue.text: The point of retirement is to live with little money keeping afloat at the end

parts.note: to be is to exist or live

indicators.note: keeping means the coin holds a letter inside it

parts.note: a dime is a US ten-cent coin, a small sum

indicators.note: at the end means take the last letter of afloat

explanation.surface: Retiring means living with a modest pension while staying solvent at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retirement' looks like leaving work; here it is retiring to bed. 'keeping' puts T, the end of 'afloat', inside DIME.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedtime is the hour when one retires for the night, so the moment of retiring.

clue.text: Suspects given Tango — it's consumed by Northerners

indicators.note: consumed by means swallowed inside the people named

parts.note: the Inuit are peoples of the Arctic north, here pluralised
Tango is T in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Arctic peoples are thought to be guilty after drinking a fizzy orange called Tango.
explanation.walkthrough: Tango is also a British orange soft drink, the surface sense. 'Suspects' is a verb: senses something.
explanation.definitionFit: To intuit is to sense something without proof, which is what one does in suspecting it.

clue.text: Sense I'm out to give you punishment?

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of their order

parts.note: the apostrophe is dropped, leaving I and M

explanation.surface: Someone senses they are being made to suffer for something.
explanation.definitionFit: Nemesis is retributive justice, named after the Greek goddess of vengeance, so a deserved downfall.

clue.text: We sat around in glow

indicators.note: around means the letters are moved round into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: People sitting round in a warm glow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'glow' is used in its sense of a heated flush, as after exertion.
explanation.definitionFit: To glow can mean to be hot and flushed, and sweating is that same body response.

clue.text: Examiner's car rubbish reversing

parts.note: Audi is a German make of car

indicators.note: reversing means the word for rubbish is turned back to front

parts.note: rot is nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: An inspector's car is a wreck going backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An auditor inspects an organisation's accounts, so is a financial examiner.

clue.text: Change ten euros, dropping the last on the road

indicators.note: change means the letters are changed around into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: dropping the last means the final letter of euros is lost

explanation.surface: An instruction to exchange some currency while travelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping the last' removes the S of EUROS, and 'Change' rearranges TEN plus EURO.
explanation.definitionFit: En route is French for on the way, so travelling or on the road.

clue.text: Opening sign

definitions.meaning: opening as an adjective means first or beginning
to sign is to mark a document with one's letters

explanation.surface: A signal that something is starting.
explanation.definitionFit: Initial means first in order, and to initial a document is to sign it with abbreviated letters.

clue.text: Eleven others played with seconds, with no duck yet

indicators.note: played means the letters are performed in a different arrangement
with no means a letter is left out

parts.note: taken as written
in cricket a duck is a score of nothing, shown as O

explanation.surface: A cricket team played the rest, with a reserve side, and nobody yet out for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a batsman's score of zero in cricket. 'with no duck' drops the O from ELEVENOTHERS, S is added, and 'played' rearranges the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Nevertheless means however or even so, which is what yet means as a conjunction.
